+    @property
+    def readable_pin(self) -> str | None:
+        """Return the PIN string if it is readable, otherwise ``None``."""
+        return self.pin if self.is_readable else None
+
+    def matches(self, pin: str) -> bool:
+        """Return True when the credential is a known PIN equal to ``pin``."""
+        return self.is_readable and self.pin == pin
+
+    def as_label(self) -> str | SlotCode:
+        """
+        Return a stable serialization for diagnostics / websocket output.
+
+        Readable credentials surface the raw PIN string so the caller can
+        mask it consistently; non-readable credentials surface the matching
+        :class:`SlotCode` sentinel.
+        """
+        if not self.present:
+            return SlotCode.EMPTY
+        if self.pin is None:
+            return SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE
+        return self.pin
+
+
+_EMPTY_CREDENTIAL = SlotCredential(present=False, pin=None)
+_UNREADABLE_CREDENTIAL = SlotCredential(present=True, pin=None)
+
+

288	    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:
289	        """
290	        Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes.
291	
292	        Schlage PINs are write-only (returned as masked values), so occupied
293	        slots return SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE and cleared slots return SlotCode.EMPTY.
294	
295	        This method only reads and classifies codes; auto-tagging of unmanaged
296	        codes is handled by ``_async_tag_unmanaged_codes()``.
297	        """
298	        managed_slots = self.managed_slots
299	        if not managed_slots:
300	            return {}
301	
302	        codes = await self._async_get_codes()
303	
304	        # Track which managed slots have tagged codes
305	        occupied_slots: set[int] = set()
306	
307	        # Collect tagged codes: keep the first per slot (sorted by code_id for determinism)
308	        tagged: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
309	        for code_id, code_data in codes.items():
310	            name = code_data.get("name", "")
311	            slot_num, friendly_name = _parse_tag(name)
312	            if slot_num is not None:
313	                tagged.append((code_id, slot_num, friendly_name))
314	
315	        tagged.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
316	        seen_slots: set[int] = set()
317	        for code_id, slot_num, friendly_name in tagged:
318	            if slot_num not in managed_slots:
319	                LOGGER.debug(
320	                    "Lock %s: ignoring tagged code slot %d outside managed range",
321	                    self.lock.entity_id,
322	                    slot_num,
323	                )
324	                continue
325	            if slot_num in seen_slots:
326	                LOGGER.warning(
327	                    "Lock %s: duplicate tag for slot %d (code_id=%s, name='%s'), "
328	                    "skipping in favor of earlier entry",
329	                    self.lock.entity_id,
330	                    slot_num,
331	                    code_id,
332	                    friendly_name,
333	                )
334	                continue
335	            seen_slots.add(slot_num)
336	            occupied_slots.add(slot_num)
337	
338	        # Build final result: UNREADABLE_CODE for occupied, EMPTY for unoccupied managed slots
339	        return {
340	            slot: SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE if slot in occupied_slots else SlotCode.EMPTY
341	            for slot in managed_slots
342	        }

392	    def calculate_in_sync(self, slot_state: SlotState) -> bool:
393	        """
394	        Calculate whether slot should be in sync.
395	
396	        Active (state=ON): PIN should match code on lock.
397	        Inactive (state=OFF): Code on lock should be empty.
398	
399	        For UNKNOWN codes (masked/write-only): in sync only if the configured
400	        PIN matches what we last successfully set. This ensures that PIN
401	        changes trigger a re-set even when the lock code is unreadable, and
402	        that taking over a slot with an existing masked code triggers a set.
403	        """
404	        lock_code = (
405	            slot_state.coordinator_code
406	            if slot_state.coordinator_code is not None
407	            else slot_state.code_state
408	        )
409	        if slot_state.active_state == STATE_ON:
410	            if lock_code is SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE:
411	                return slot_state.pin_state == self._last_set_pin
412	            if lock_code is SlotCode.EMPTY:
413	                # If we recently set a PIN on this slot and it matches the
414	                # configured PIN, trust the set — the provider may not have
415	                # caught up yet (eventual consistency, e.g. Schlage cloud API).
416	                return (
417	                    self._last_set_pin is not None
418	                    and slot_state.pin_state == self._last_set_pin
419	                )
420	            return slot_state.pin_state == lock_code
421	        # active_state == STATE_OFF: slot should be cleared
422	        # The "" check covers the fallback path where coordinator_code is None
423	        # and lock_code comes from the code sensor entity state (which returns ""
424	        # for SlotCode.EMPTY).
425	        return lock_code is SlotCode.EMPTY or lock_code == ""

{
  "command": "gh pr create --base refactor/entity-to-tick --title \"refactor(data-model): replace SlotCode with SlotCredential value type\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Proposed change\n\nResolves the audit's \"three meanings, one value\" collapse on coordinator data. Introduces an explicit `SlotCredential` value type and migrates every consumer (coordinator, all 7 providers, sync, sensor, diagnostics, websocket, config flow) plus the test infrastructure.\n\n### Concern 1 (audit #10): `dict[int, str | SlotCode]` → `dict[int, SlotCredential]`\n\n`SlotCredential` (in `models.py`) is a frozen, slotted dataclass with three constructors:\n- `empty()` — slot is cleared on the lock\n- `unreadable()` — slot holds a write-only code (Matter, Schlage)\n- `known(pin)` — slot holds a code whose value the provider exposes\n\nAccessors: `is_empty`, `is_present`, `is_readable`, `readable_pin`, `matches(pin)`, `as_label()` (returns `str | SlotCode` for diagnostics/websocket back-compat).\n\n`SlotCode` enum is kept for the as-label serialization path so external consumers (diagnostics output, websocket payloads) see the same `\"empty\"` / `\"unreadable_code\"` strings as before.\n\n### Concern 2 (audit #8): resolve `get_expected_pin`'s `None` triple-meaning\n\n`coordinator.get_expected_pin()` → `coordinator.desired_credential(slot_num) -> SlotCredential`. Disabled OR no-PIN-configured both yield `SlotCredential.empty()`; enabled-with-PIN yields `SlotCredential.known(pin)`. Callers that wanted the boolean form use `desired_credential(...).is_present` (via the kept `slot_expects_pin`).\n\n`sync.py` `SlotState.coordinator_code: SlotCredential | None`; `calculate_in_sync` rewritten with credential accessors. Single read path for \"desired state\" is now the coordinator-via-config side (the entity-state fallback only kicks in when `coordinator_code is None` — i.e., no data yet).\n\n### Concern 3 (audit #20): base `push_update` helper\n\nNew `BaseLock._push_credential_update(code_slot, credential)` lifts the `if self.coordinator: self.coordinator.push_update({slot: value})` boilerplate that five providers each implemented. All optimistic set/clear updates and push-event handlers in Z-Wave JS, Matter, ZHA, Z2M, and Virtual go through this helper now.\n\n### Per-provider mapping (concern #1)\n\n| Provider | `async_get_usercodes` builds |\n|---|---|\n| Akuvox | `known(pin)` for tagged users with PIN; `empty()` otherwise |\n| Schlage | `unreadable()` for occupied (write-only); `empty()` otherwise |\n| Matter | `unreadable()` for occupied; `empty()` for unoccupied managed slots |\n| Z-Wave JS | `known(value)` for plain PIN, `unreadable()` for masked, `empty()` for cleared (asymmetric `in_use` checks preserved) |\n| ZHA | `known(pin_code)` when status=Enabled, `empty()` for available, `unreadable()` on read failure |\n| Zigbee2MQTT | `known(pin)` for enabled+PIN, `empty()` for absent/disabled, `unreadable()` for publish/timeout/read failure |\n| Virtual | `known(stored_code)` for stored, `empty()` for managed-but-not-stored |\n\n## Out-of-scope findings worth flagging for G\n\n- `providers/_base.py:563` and four other sites use the Py3 tuple-expression `except E1, E2:` (without parens). Functional but stylistically inconsistent with the parenthesized form used elsewhere. Worth normalizing in G.\n- `sensor.py.native_value` reaches into `coordinator.desired_credential(...).readable_pin` to surface the configured PIN for write-only providers (functionally equivalent to the prior behavior, but architecturally a layer-cross). G could consider hoisting that fallback.\n\n## Type of change\n\n- [ ] Dependency upgrade\n- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)\n- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)\n- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)\n- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests\n\n## Additional information\n\nFinal PR in the resilience refactor chain except G (god-module cleanup). Depends on #1191 (entity-to-tick). The base of this PR is intentionally `refactor/entity-to-tick`; once #1191 merges, GitHub will auto-retarget to main.\n\n- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #\n- This PR is related to issue:\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Open F PR targeting D branch"
}

230	    async def async_request_active_toggle(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
231	        """
232	        Apply an enabled/disabled toggle requested by the switch entity.
233	
234	        Disable is unconditional. Enable validates that a PIN exists and
235	        raises ``PinRequiredError`` if absent (the switch translates
236	        that into ``HomeAssistantError``). On a successful enable the
237	        ``pin_required`` repair issue is cleared; failures inside the
238	        issue registry are logged and do not unwind the write.
239	        """
240	        if not enabled:
241	            self._write_config(CONF_ENABLED, False)
242	            return
243	
244	        if not self.pin_value:
245	            self._safely_raise_pin_required_issue()
246	            raise PinRequiredError(
247	                f"Set a PIN code for slot {self._slot_num} before enabling it"
248	            )
249	
250	        self._write_config(CONF_ENABLED, True)
251	        try:
252	            async_delete_issue(
253	                self._hass,
254	                DOMAIN,
255	                f"pin_required_{self._config_entry.entry_id}_{self._slot_num}",
256	            )
257	        except Exception:
258	            _LOGGER.exception(
259	                "%s: Failed to delete pin_required repair issue after enable",
260	                self._log_prefix,
261	            )

264	
265	    @callback
266	    def notify_config_changed(self) -> None:
267	        """
268	        React to a config entry change.
269	
270	        Called by ``async_update_listener`` after it refreshes
271	        ``runtime_data.config``. Updates the condition-entity subscription
272	        if the condition entity moved, recomputes derived state, and
273	        fans the new state out to writers and sync managers.
274	        """
275	        if not self._started:
276	            return
277	        self._update_condition_subscription()
278	        self._recompute_active()
279	        self._notify_state_subscribers()

289	        """Write one slot field to the config entry."""

292	    @callback
293	    def _write_config_fields(self, fields: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
294	        """
295	        Write one or more slot fields to the config entry in a single update.
296	
297	        Coalescing avoids the trap where the update listener has not yet
298	        refreshed ``runtime_data.config`` between two consecutive writes,
299	        leading the second write to drop the first.
300	
301	        ``async_update_entry`` schedules the update listener as a task,
302	        so ``runtime_data.config`` is still stale at the synchronous
303	        notify below. Refresh it eagerly here so ``_recompute_active``,
304	        ``_notify_state_subscribers``, and ``_poke_sync_managers``

  "new_string": "async def test_poke_sync_managers_isolates_individual_failures(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    mock_lock_config_entry,\n    lock_code_manager_config_entry,\n    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,\n):\n    \"\"\"One raising sync manager does not abort the poke of the others.\"\"\"\n    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data\n    coordinator = runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]\n\n    # Inject two stand-in managers so the poke loop has predictable\n    # targets regardless of how many real sync managers ended up wired\n    # to this slot via the fixture entity registrations.\n    boom = RuntimeError(\"simulated sync manager poke failure\")\n    healthy_called = {\"value\": False}\n\n    class _StandIn:\n        def __init__(self, raise_on_call: bool) -> None:\n            self._raise = raise_on_call\n\n        def request_sync_check(self) -> None:\n            if self._raise:\n                raise boom\n            healthy_called[\"value\"] = True\n\n    failing = _StandIn(raise_on_call=True)\n    healthy = _StandIn(raise_on_call=False)\n    coordinator._sync_managers.add(failing)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n    coordinator._sync_managers.add(healthy)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n\n    try:\n        with caplog.at_level(logging.ERROR):\n            coordinator._poke_sync_managers()\n    finally:\n        coordinator._sync_managers.discard(failing)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n        coordinator._sync_managers.discard(healthy)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n\n    assert healthy_called[\"value\"] is True\n    assert any(\n        record.exc_info is not None and record.exc_info[1] is boom\n        for record in caplog.records\n        if record.levelname == \"ERROR\"\n    )"

{
  "command": "git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nrefactor(entity): hoist slot-coordinator caching to BaseLockCodeManagerEntity\n\nEach entity platform (text, switch, both binary sensors) was\nre-resolving the slot coordinator from ``runtime_data.slot_coordinators``\non every call. The lookup is cheap but the duplicated null check, the\ninconsistent \"missing coordinator\" handling, and the divergent\n``async_added_to_hass`` boilerplate were all paying rent.\n\nHoist:\n\n* ``BaseLockCodeManagerEntity._slot_coordinator: SlotEntityCoordinator\n  | None`` -- attribute initialized to ``None``, resolved once in the\n  base's ``async_added_to_hass``. Lifecycle is safe because slot\n  removal tears down the entity and re-adding the slot creates a new\n  entity bound to the new coordinator, so the cached reference never\n  goes stale.\n* ``_register_slot_coordinator_subscription`` -- single hook the base\n  calls right after the resolution. > AGENT

Pushed `21fb1614` to PR #1191.

**Two improvements landed in one commit:**

1. **Slot-coordinator caching hoisted to `BaseLockCodeManagerEntity`**:
   - `_slot_coordinator: SlotEntityCoordinator | None` attribute on the base
   - Resolved once in the base's `async_added_to_hass`
   - Single `_register_slot_coordinator_subscription` hook with state-subscriber default
   - Missing-coordinator WARNING centralized
   - Subclasses just override the hook for non-default subscription shapes:
     - `LockCodeManagerActiveEntity` → `register_active_view`
     - `LockCodeManagerCodeSlotInSyncEntity` → `register_sync_manager`

2. **+9 coverage tests** addressing both the test-analyzer's deferred items AND the previously untested defensive fixes from `3448b835`:
   - Slot remove → re-add lifecycle (fresh coordinator)
   - `request_sync_check` public-wrapper contract
   - Active binary sensor doesn't self-track state
   - Eager `runtime_data.config` refresh observable to subscribers
   - Unload continues when coordinator stop raises
   - `register_active_view` immediate writer failure propagates + discards
   - Repair-issue delete failure doesn't unwind enable
   - `_handle_condition_state_change` `_started` guard
   - `_poke_sync_managers` per-manager isolation

**965 tests pass; prek fully clean** (ruff, ruff-format, pydocstyle, mypy, flake8 all green this time).

Lifecycle invariant the hoist relies on: slot removed → entity removed → no calls to stale ref; slot re-added → new coordinator → new entity → fresh ref. This holds because `__init__.py` creates the coordinator first then the entities (D's design), and slot removal stops+pops the coordinator before/around entity removal.

2. **No coverage of the missing-coordinator branch** (test-analyzer): the production code's WARNING fallback in `entity.py:232-238` has zero tests.

**Important (worth fixing):**
3. **`assert self._slot_coordinator is not None`** strippable under `python -O`. Replace with explicit raise or document as type-narrowing.
4. **WARNING → ERROR** when coordinator missing — entities-that-exist-but-do-nothing is a debugging trap.
5. **Hook-dispatch-by-entity-type test missing**: no test proves text/switch land in `_state_subscribers`, active in `_active_view_writers`, in-sync in `_sync_managers`.
6. **`test_active_binary_sensor_does_not_self_track_state` too narrow**: only catches `_condition_*` / `_config_entry_*` attribute patterns; a regression using `_unsub_state_change` slips through.
7. **`test_write_config_fields_refreshes_runtime_config_before_notify` could be stronger**: assert *first* observation is "5555", not just all.
8. **Tighten `_register_slot_coordinator_subscription` docstring** lead-in (state subscribers fire only after config writes, not all coordinator state changes).

**Deferring:**
- `_register_slot_coordinator_subscription` as `@abstractmethod` — default is deliberate convenience for text/switch; making it abstract forces opt-in everywhere.
- 4-line lifecycle comment compression — load-bearing as written.
- `_poke_sync_managers` iteration-order polish (small).

A method (vs decorator) is cleaner here because it returns the narrowed type — call sites get `coord = self._require_slot_coordinator()` with mypy knowing it's non-None. A decorator would need to either thread the coordinator through `**kwargs` or have the wrapped method re-read `self._slot_coordinator` anyway.

505	async def test_write_config_fields_refreshes_runtime_config_before_notify(
506	    hass: HomeAssistant,
507	    mock_lock_config_entry,
508	    lock_code_manager_config_entry,
509	):
510	    """A synchronous notify after async_update_entry sees the fresh config.
511	
512	    ``async_update_entry`` schedules the listener as a task, so
513	    ``runtime_data.config`` is still stale at the synchronous
514	    ``_notify_state_subscribers`` call inside ``_write_config_fields``.
515	    Subscribers must observe the post-write value, not the pre-write one.
516	    """
517	    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data
518	    coordinator = runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
519	
520	    captured_pin: list[str | None] = []
521	
522	    def capture_subscriber() -> None:
523	        captured_pin.append(coordinator.pin_value)
524	
525	    unsub = coordinator.register_state_subscriber(capture_subscriber)
526	    try:
527	        await coordinator.async_request_pin_update("5555")
528	        await hass.async_block_till_done()
529	    finally:
530	        unsub()
531	
532	    # The subscriber fires twice: once synchronously after the eager refresh
533	    # inside _write_config_fields, and once when the listener task re-runs
534	    # notify_config_changed. Both reads must observe the post-write value;
535	    # without the eager refresh the first would be the stale pre-write PIN.
536	    assert captured_pin
537	    assert all(pin == "5555" for pin in captured_pin)
538

  "new_string": "async def test_active_binary_sensor_does_not_self_track_state(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    mock_lock_config_entry,\n):\n    \"\"\"``LockCodeManagerActiveEntity`` must not subscribe to the condition entity itself.\n\n    The slot coordinator owns the condition-entity subscription. This variant covers\n    the raise-before-cleanup mode -- proving the registry is cleared\n    regardless of how stop fails.\n    \"\"\"\n    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data\n    failing = next(iter(runtime_data.slot_coordinators.values()))\n    boom = RuntimeError(\"simulated coordinator stop failure (before cleanup)\")\n\n    def failing_stop() -> None:\n        # Do NOT call the real stop -- raise immediately so internal\n        # state is left intact, simulating a stop that fails at its\n        # very first statement.\n        raise boom\n\n    with patch.object(failing, \"async_stop\", failing_stop):\n        with caplog.at_level(logging.ERROR):\n            await hass.config_entries.async_unload(\n                lock_code_manager_config_entry.entry_id\n            )\n            await hass.async_block_till_done()\n\n    assert runtime_data.slot_coordinators == {}\n    assert any(\n        record.exc_info is not None and record.exc_info[1] is boom\n        for record in caplog.records\n        if record.levelname == \"ERROR\"\n    )"

> AGENT

Pushed `ac85a377`. Summary of what landed:

**Critical fixes:**
- **`text.py` asymmetry resolved** — hoisted `_require_slot_coordinator` to base; both text and switch now raise `HomeAssistantError` on missing coordinator instead of one raising and the other silently logging.
- **WARNING → ERROR** on missing-coordinator at add time, with a comment explaining the internal-inconsistency intent.

**Polish:**
- `_register_slot_coordinator_subscription` docstring tightened to match actual contract.
- `assert self._slot_coordinator is not None` now has explicit "this is type-narrowing" notes.

**4 new tests + 2 strengthened:**
- `test_base_entity_caches_slot_coordinator_on_add` — pins the hoist contract (entity instance's cached coord is the runtime_data instance).
- `test_hook_dispatch_routes_each_entity_kind_to_the_right_collection` — text/switch in `_state_subscribers`, active in `_active_view_writers`.
- `test_text_set_value_raises_when_slot_coordinator_missing` — pins the new symmetric raise behavior.
- `test_unload_clears_registry_when_coordinator_stop_raises_before_cleanup` — the raise-before-cleanup variant.
- *Strengthened* `test_write_config_fields_refreshes_runtime_config_before_notify` — asserts the *first* observation is "5555" (the load-bearing invariant).
- *Strengthened* `test_active_binary_sensor_does_not_self_track_state` — replaced attribute-regex with a behavioral check (one condition-state flip → exactly one active-view fire = no duplicate subscription).

**One pre-existing D-design limitation surfaced** (test docstring flags it for G): in-sync per-lock entities are added via a separate adder path that fires *before* the slot coordinator exists on initial setup, so their `register_sync_manager` registration is unreachable in the normal path. Works fine on options-flow re-adds. Worth flagging for follow-up but not a regression introduced by this PR.

**969 tests pass; prek fully clean** (ruff, ruff-format, pydocstyle, mypy, flake8 all green).

Real hazards live at await points and lifecycle seams.\n- Bound methods don't have stable identity: `obj.method is obj.method` returns False. Don't use `is` to verify \"method wasn't patched\" — assert behavior instead.\n- Task lifecycle: coroutine `finally` runs *before* the Task transitions to `done()`. So `_tick_tasks.discard(task)` in finally always runs before any external observer sees `task.done()=True`. \"Task that just completed could be in the registry\" is impossible.\n- Tests that patch teardown methods (`async_stop`, etc.) to raise must still call the original first or leak resources (HA test harness flags lingering timers).\n- HA service-call layer reclassifies exceptions raised by service handlers. Mocks raising `LockDisconnected` get re-wrapped as `LockOperationFailed` by the base. Patch private provider methods (e.g. `_async_add_code`) instead of registering handler mocks if you need a specific exception type to flow through.\n- HA's `async_update_entry` schedules the update listener as a task — `runtime_data.config` is STALE at the synchronous notify that immediately follows. Eager refresh (`runtime_data.config = EntryConfig.from_entry(...)`) is needed before sync notify if entities are to observe the post-write value.\n- `await` on an immediately-returning coroutine yields once to the loop, which lets other pending tasks run. Test assertions about \"first observation should be X\" must run BEFORE `await hass.async_block_till_done()` to catch the synchronous notify before the listener task fires.\n- `hass.bus.async_listeners()` returns `dict[str, int]` (count per event type), NOT a dict of lists. Their `register_sync_manager` registration with the slot coordinator is unreachable on initial setup; the registration only happens for slots added via the options-flow `_async_setup_new_locks` path. This means `SlotEntityCoordinator._poke_sync_managers` is effectively a no-op for entries set up via initial entry setup. Cleaner than half-finishing.\n- **Bulk sed for mechanical type-substitution migrations.** When introducing a new value type that replaces a tagged union (str | SlotCode → SlotCredential), 80% of the work is mechanical. Find-replace via sed in tests, hand-edit the ~10% that have compound literals or tricky equality assertions.\n- **Tests for defensive fixes are mandatory, not optional.** Round-1 fixes on PR D landed without regression tests. Introduce `SlotEntityCoordinator`\n\nNew per-`(config_entry, slot)` coordinator in `slot_manager.py` that owns:\n- The derived \"active\" state (computed from `enabled` + condition entity) and the `inactive_because_of` attribute.\n- The condition-entity subscription itself.\n- Slot-level repair-issue lifecycle (`pin_required` create/delete).\n- Three intent dispatchers that entities call: `async_request_name_update`, `async_request_pin_update`, `async_request_active_toggle`. These coalesce the config write (`_write_config_fields` accepts a dict so empty-PIN auto-disable is one combined write rather than two — closing a stale-`runtime_data.config` race) and poke each lock's `SlotSyncManager.request_sync_check()` so the next tick reconciles.\n\nEntities collapse to thin views:\n- `LockCodeManagerActiveEntity` (binary sensor) goes from ~150 to ~25 lines; the config-entry update listener and condition-entity subscription move to the coordinator.\n- `text.py` `async_set_value` calls `coordinator.async_request_pin_update / name_update`. No more `_enabled_entity_id`, registry-string sibling lookup, or direct `async_disable_slot` import.\n- `switch.py` `async_turn_on/off` call `coordinator.async_request_active_toggle`. No more `_pin_entity_id`, sibling registry lookups, or inline repair-issue management.\n\nThe per-lock `SlotSyncManager` is unchanged in role; it now exposes `request_sync_check()` as a public verb so the slot coordinator can nudge sync without reaching into `_request_sync_check`.\n\n### 2. Hoist slot-coordinator caching to `BaseLockCodeManagerEntity`\n\nEvery entity platform was re-resolving `runtime_data.slot_coordinators.get(self.slot_num)` on every method call with duplicated null checks. Hoisted to the base:\n\n- `_slot_coordinator: SlotEntityCoordinator | None` attribute initialized in `__init__`, resolved once in the base's `async_added_to_hass`. Lifecycle is safe because slot removal tears down the entity, and re-adding the slot creates a new entity bound to the new coordinator — the cached reference never goes stale.\n- `_register_slot_coordinator_subscription` hook on the base with a state-subscriber default (the shape text and switch want). `LockCodeManagerActiveEntity` overrides to register the active view; `LockCodeManagerCodeSlotInSyncEntity` overrides to register the per-lock sync manager.\n- `_require_slot_coordinator` helper on the base for intent paths. text and switch both call it so a missing coordinator surfaces as `HomeAssistantError` rather than the prior asymmetric behavior (text silently logged WARNING and returned; switch raised).\n- Missing-coordinator at add time logs ERROR with a comment explaining the internal-inconsistency intent.\n\n### 3. `curr_slots` fix (deferred from #1187 review)\n\n`async_unload_entry`'s `curr_slots = config_entry.data.get(CONF_SLOTS, {})` returned `{}` for any normally-loaded entry because `_setup_entry_after_start` migrates `data → options` at first setup. Replaced with `list(get_entry_config(config_entry).slots)` so the entity-removers actually fire on unload. Slot coordinators are stopped after the entity removers (so `async_will_remove_from_hass` can still unregister cleanly) and cleared from `runtime_data`. The stop loop tolerates per-coordinator failures (logged at ERROR; registry cleared regardless).\n\n### 4. Coordinator-error isolation and defensive fixes (round 1 review)\n\n- Eager `runtime_data.config = EntryConfig.from_entry(...)` refresh after `async_update_entry` so the synchronous notify observes the post-write value, not the stale pre-write one (`async_update_entry` schedules the listener as a task, so the listener's refresh hasn't run yet).\n- `register_active_view` immediate writer call now wraps the initial fire in try/except, logs and discards the writer if it raises, then re-raises so the platform rejects the half-added entity cleanly.\n- `async_request_active_toggle` repair-issue create and delete each wrapped in try/except so a registry failure doesn't unwind the config write or mask the actual outcome.\n- `_handle_condition_state_change` guards on `_started` so late-firing callbacks against a torn-down coordinator no-op.\n- `_poke_sync_managers` per-manager try/except so one raising manager doesn't abort the loop.\n- Unload paths use `pop` / `list(...)` and per-coordinator try/except so a raising stop is logged and the registry is cleared either way.\n\n### 5. Test coverage\n\n`tests/test_slot_manager.py` grew from 10 tests in the original PR to 28 across three review rounds:\n- Lifecycle: slot add/remove/re-add produces a fresh coordinator instance with fresh fields, condition-entity swap re-subscribes.\n- Hoist contract: `_slot_coordinator` is populated on add; text/switch land in `_state_subscribers`; active sensor lands in `_active_view_writers`; text raises `HomeAssistantError` when coordinator missing.\n- Defensive fixes each pinned by a regression test (writer raise on registration, repair-issue delete failure, condition-state guard, sync-manager isolation, unload-with-stop-raises in two variants, eager-refresh observable to subscribers).\n- Behavioral check that the active binary sensor doesn't re-introduce entity-side condition tracking (a condition-entity state flip produces exactly one active-view fire).\n\n### Out-of-scope findings worth flagging\n\n- `slot_disabled` and `slot_suspended` repair issues still live in `SlotSyncManager._disable_slot / _suspend_slot` because they're per-lock-slot events emitted from the tick. Moving them under the slot coordinator would invert the layering. Flag for PR F if the data-model rewrite revisits issue ownership.\n- **In-sync per-lock entities are added via a separate adder path (`__init__.py:829`) that fires BEFORE the slot coordinator exists on initial setup.** Their `register_sync_manager` registration with the slot coordinator is unreachable on initial setup; it only happens for slots added via the options-flow `_async_setup_new_locks` path. This means `SlotEntityCoordinator._poke_sync_managers` is effectively a no-op for entries set up via initial entry setup. Depends on #1187 (lifecycle hygiene), #1188 (lock ownership), #1189 (single breaker mutator). Interacts cleanly with #1190 (no provider overlap). #1192 (data-model rewrite) is stacked on top of this branch and will auto-retarget to main when this lands. G (god-module cleanup) remains.\n\n- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #\n- This PR is related to issue:\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",
